sources.title: On the Origin of Species — 1859 first edition, introduction
sources.author: Charles Darwin; edition prepared by John van Wyhe and Sue Asscher
sources.note: Darwin explains evidence accumulation, Wallace’s parallel discovery, and the need to explain adaptation. He acknowledges incomplete documentation and counterevidence; the hosted first edition provides an English text.

targets.A: Scientific argument and verified historical English edition.
targets.N: Primary scientific nonfiction; argument structure, not an independent reception vote.

sources.limits: Selected passages only; historical theory must not be treated as a current biology textbook.

sources.title: Rachel Carson (1907–1964)
sources.note: Connects Silent Spring’s ecological synthesis and public-facing prose with environmental mobilization, while describing industrial opposition. Its celebratory account requires comparison with more qualified causal histories.

targets.A: Science writing and public reception beyond literary and philosophical canons.
targets.N: Environmental nonfiction, explanatory writing and historical reception.

sources.location: Silent Spring and Quiet Courage sections
sources.limits: Retrospective institutional account; influence is not attributable to one book alone.

sources.title: Silent Spring — Edward O. Wilson’s 2002 afterword
sources.publisher: Mariner Books / Houghton Mifflin; FAO-hosted excerpt
sources.author: Edward O. Wilson
sources.note: Wilson credits Carson’s synthesis of scattered research, clarifies her opposition to reckless broad-spectrum spraying, and cautions that the book’s influence mingled with other scientific and activist efforts.

targets.A: Scientific synthesis and limits on claims of singular historical influence.
targets.N: Scientist’s retrospective evaluation of environmental nonfiction.

sources.location: Afterword pp.357–362; edition imprint PDF p.2
sources.limits: One underlying afterword, not an additional FAO judgment. PDF is a 33-page excerpt, not the complete book.

sources.title: Carlo Greppi, the Italian writer who brings Primo Levi’s savior back to life
sources.note: Uses Perrone’s assistance to discuss dignity and moral agency in Levi’s testimony.
sources.limits: Profile excerpt, not a full comparative review of Levi.

sources.title: Five History Books Recommended by You
sources.note: Members recommend Bloch’s accessible reflections on historical method and Trouillot’s treatment of power and historical silencing. Other selections cover memory, gender and antimodernism.

targets.A: Reconsultation expands candidate mapping; original record preserved.
targets.N: Historical method, memory and power, with member reception evidence.
